encoder: a single Sonnet 5.5 agent working alone from the brief (no subagents, no other encoding read)
display_name: Employment Claims Act 2016 (Singapore), whole, with an employee-seat layer
seat: an employee, or a former employee, with a salary-related claim against an employer, asking on facts they can state whether they may bring it to the tribunal, in what time, with what steps and at what cost, and what follows
edition: Employment Claims Act 2016, 2020 Revised Edition, informal consolidation in force from 1 April 2025, as the converter rendering inputs/ECA2016.txt (sha256 1db5f66cea35b25f27524417d97cc95a6d07c9a9399eb5d0e63e6e5100d1b596); the rendering is not the official text

scope.encoded: every operative provision: ss 2 to 7 (s 3(6)(b) included), ss 8 to 31 and 35(2), the First to Fourth Schedules (one entry per item), and the 29 defined terms of s 2(1); 92 seat questions over them
scope.not_encoded: reason 1 (not operative): title page, arrangement of sections, long title, enacting words, headings, Legislative History, Comparative Table; reason 2 (machinery, each row stating its gap): s 1, ss 3(6)(a) and (c) to (g), 3(7), 4(6), 12(8), 18(5), 32, 33, 34, 35(1). Fees, claim limits, periods, forms and prescribed classes that regulations or Rules of Court set are inputs; no figure is taken from memory
scope.coverage: see NOTES.md, Coverage: one row per section, subsection, paragraph, sub-paragraph, schedule item, defined term and heading; 585 rows, every non-blank line of the text in exactly one row

checks.note: check.sh on the main builds named below: 1150 assertions satisfied, 0 failed, 0 refused, 0 errors over 17 modules, with the same four counts on both builds; the same satisfied counts on the unstable build; srcrefs.py 0 problems; coverage.py, kinds.py, jural.py and seatcheck.py clean (all printed in NOTES.md). Run 2026-11-05, after the revision for the ruling of that date.

not_reviewed: No domain expert has read this against the text. It was written and checked by one agent with the diagnostics only; the readings marked for a lawyer in NOTES.md (Marginal readings for a lawyer, forks F1, F6, F7, F8, F9, F10, F11, and the ten open questions Q1 to Q10) have not been ruled on by a lawyer, and the text it encodes is an unofficial converter rendering.
rulings: E1 (2026-11-04): per-section answers; gathering by hand only where it helps a reader
N2 (2026-11-04): a flat negative counts as the text's no

2026-11-05 (Meng): "i agree with your lean: no for a and b; nothing for c." (a) a period the text fixes in its own words: JUST FALSE outside it; (b) a "where" condition not met: JUST FALSE; (c) a scope limit with no "only": NOTHING outside the scope. Assumed, not ruled: "when", "upon" and "whenever" read as "where" (fork F9)

interpretation_act_time_module.why_not_used: it has no rule for a period of months or years, and none for a period 'after' an event, and answers NOTHING for both; the month-end fork F6 is therefore not answered by it, and fork F7 is agreed by its s 50(a) for 'from' but not decided for 'after'
interpretation_act_time_module.gap_not_modelled: s 50(b), (c) and (d): a last day that is a Sunday or a public holiday moves to the next day; layer 1 takes no Sunday or public-holiday input, so s 3(2), s 12(6) and s 22(10) answer JUST FALSE for an act done on the next working day; to fill later
interpretation_act_time_module.note: the staged copy carries a 3-line header; with the first 3 lines removed, git hash-object gives the blob above

other_acts.name: Employment Act 1968
other_acts.what_the_encoding_takes_as_input: `salary` and `workman` as s 2(1) of that Act gives them (yes/no/unsure inputs of the s 2(1) definitions here); the Commissioner for Labour appointed under its s 3(1) and an authorised person appointed under its s 3(3); the last day of the period in its s 65(2A), as extended under s 65(2B) (an input of `s 3(2)(a)`); the dismissals of its s 14(1) and (2) and s 84(1) and (2) (yes/no inputs of s 27(2)(a) to (d); paragraphs (d) and (e) of s 3(2) are tied to claims under its s 14(2) and s 84(2)); the item names of the Schedules, which are named constructors

other_acts.name: Retirement and Re-employment Act 1993
other_acts.what_the_encoding_takes_as_input: `employment assistance payment` as its s 2(1) gives it (an input of the s 2(1) definition); representations under its s 8(1) and s 8B(1) (yes/no inputs of s 16(3), (5) and (7)); the dispute of its s 8A(3) and the last day determined under its s 8B(8) (inputs of s 3(2)(b) and (c)); the guidelines issued under its s 11B (an input of the s 2(1) definition)

other_acts.name: Industrial Relations Act 1960

other_acts.name: State Courts Act 1970
